clue.text: One elects to put a cross on it

definitions.text: One elects to put a cross on it

parts.words: One elects to put a cross on it
parts.note: reads like a riddle about a person choosing to mark something; the 'it' is the sheet a voter marks with an X when choosing a candidate

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone choosing to mark something with a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: In elections a voter marks a printed form with an X beside the chosen candidate.

clue.text: Author runs under fence

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first, so it is written after it

parts.note: J. M. Barrie, the Scottish author of Peter Pan
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A writer's scoring sits beneath a fence, like a batsman near the boundary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' works because this is a down entry: R is placed below BARRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a kind of obstruction that blocks passage.

clue.text: Piccalilli lacked some colour

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, so the answer lies inside the words Piccalilli lacked

explanation.surface: A jar of piccalilli, the yellow pickle relish, lacked some colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Piccalilli is a bright yellow British mustard pickle, which makes 'lacked some colour' read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale purple shade named after the flowering shrub.

clue.text: Carthorse startled musicians

indicators.note: a startled horse jumps about, so the letters of the word Carthorse are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A carthorse was frightened by a group of players.
explanation.definitionFit: A large body of instrumental players performing together.

clue.text: Course taken by a non-driver?

parts.note: suggests a learner avoiding driving lessons, but really means the route walked by a pedestrian, someone who is not in a car

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot drive picks an alternative course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A footway or track is the route someone on foot follows.

clue.text: Corny treatment?

parts.note: corny seems to mean trite, but here it means to do with corns on the feet, so the treatment is foot care

explanation.surface: A complaint that some handling of a subject is trite.
explanation.definitionFit: Care of the feet and toenails, including removing corns, by a chiropodist.

clue.text: It ran around laughing

indicators.note: the letters of It ran are moved around into a different order

explanation.surface: Something ran about while laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare literary adjective from French, meaning cheerful or smiling.

clue.text: Carriage from part of the East End

definitions.meaning: a borough in London's East End

explanation.definitionFit: A hired horse-drawn coach shares its name with a London borough in the East End, the traditionally working-class east of the city.

clue.text: Defend top dog

definitions.meaning: to support or stand up for a cause

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to advocate for a cause; as a noun it is the title-holder who beats all rivals.

clue.text: Moved a deer and colt and put them in different places

indicators.note: the letters of a deer and colt are shifted to new positions, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone shifted a deer and a young horse, separating them.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram indicator doubles as a gloss on the definition, which makes the surface read smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: To have transferred something to a new site.

clue.text: A practitioner goes round hospital for this special purpose

indicators.note: one word encircles another, so the doctor's letters are placed around the hospital's

parts.note: a medical practitioner is a doctor, DOC

explanation.surface: A doctor makes the rounds of a hospital for a particular reason.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase literally means 'for this', which matches the definition closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase describing something arranged for one particular need only.

clue.text: Had a teasing desire then scratched?

definitions.text: Had a teasing desire then scratched?

parts.words: Had a teasing desire then scratched?
parts.note: a tickling irritation of the skin is a teasing urge, and scratching is what naturally follows it

explanation.surface: Someone felt a playful urge and then clawed at something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teasing desire' sounds flirtatious, but it is the prickly urge on the skin that makes you scratch.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly irritation of the skin prompts scratching, and the word also means being restlessly eager.

clue.text: Taxes one, one North of the Border

parts.note: a scot is an old word for a tax or levy, as in scot-free
a man is a person, someone, one

explanation.surface: A tax bill for one person living in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the Border' is the English way of saying 'in Scotland'.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Scotland, which lies beyond the English border to the north.

clue.text: Financial return

parts.note: a sum of money given back, for example on tax overpaid, rather than a profit

explanation.surface: A phrase that sounds like an investment yield.
explanation.definitionFit: A partial refund of money paid, such as excess tax handed back.

clue.text: Where one goes down for bargains

definitions.text: Where one goes down for bargains

parts.words: Where one goes down for bargains
parts.note: in a department store the cheap goods were traditionally sold on the lowest floor, reached by going downstairs

explanation.surface: A shopper heads downstairs in search of cheap deals.
explanation.definitionFit: The underground floor of a store, as in the phrase bargain basement.

clue.text: It in the convent is of first importance

indicators.note: the word It is placed inside the word for the religious house

parts.note: a priory is a house of monks or nuns, a kind of convent
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something in a nunnery matters above all else.
explanation.definitionFit: Precedence: the state of coming before everything else in rank.

clue.text: Extend beyond Andover reaching the interior

indicators.note: the answer is found in the inside part of the phrase Andover reaching, not its edges

explanation.surface: Something stretches past Andover, a town in Hampshire, into the heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: To go too far or stretch past a limit.

clue.text: However their leader in a rush was disproved

indicators.note: the pieces are set inside the word for the marsh plant

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like water plant
but means however

indicators.note: the leader of their is its first letter

explanation.surface: Their captain hurried, yet the claim was shown false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' looks like a hurry but is the plant REED; BUT plus T goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shown to be false by argument or evidence.

clue.text: Marge's so embarrassed by the very thin material

indicators.note: an embarrassed person is thrown into confusion, so the letters of Marge's so are mixed up

explanation.surface: Marge blushes because her outfit is see-through.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate gauzy fabric, or fine cobweb thread.

clue.text: Get away with Jim first reportedly in a tunic

indicators.note: the sound of Jim is placed before the escape word
what is heard rather than written: the name Jim, said out loud, matches a word for a sports hall

parts.note: a man's name, said aloud
to slip is to escape unnoticed

explanation.surface: Escaping with a man called Jim while wearing a tunic.
explanation.walkthrough: A GYMSLIP is a sleeveless pinafore dress once worn by British schoolgirls.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless pinafore dress forming part of a traditional school uniform.

clue.text: Leonard back behind marsh plant

indicators.note: the reversed name comes after the marsh word

parts.note: a fen is a low marshy area

indicators.note: the short form of the name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Len is a short form of Leonard

explanation.surface: Leonard is stuck behind a plant growing in a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marsh plant' reads as one phrase, but 'marsh' gives FEN and 'plant' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic umbelliferous herb with feathery leaves and an aniseed taste.

clue.text: Supply

parts.note: looks like the verb provide, but split it as supple plus -ly: in a flexible, nimble manner

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb of supple, meaning nimbly and flexibly.

clue.text: Impetus for a second before hesitation in speech

indicators.note: the first piece is placed ahead of the next

parts.note: a short time, an instant
um is the sound of hesitating while talking

explanation.surface: A speaker pauses briefly, losing drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving force or impulse that keeps something moving forward.

clue.text: Never-changing audacity

indicators.note: the letters of Never change places to form a new word

explanation.surface: Boldness that never alters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek or boldness, as in 'what a nerve'.

clue.text: Scare rebel leader in combat

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for combat

parts.note: a fight is a combat

indicators.note: the leader of the word rebel is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rebel commander is frightened during a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden shock of fear.

clue.text: It is hard work to turn the crank

definitions.meaning: to operate a mill by turning a handle

explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning tedious toil and a verb meaning to work a mill handle round to crush something.

clue.text: Almost split the key

indicators.note: almost all of the word is used, the last letter dropped

parts.note: cleft means split

explanation.surface: Someone nearly broke the key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like a door key but is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the sign at the start of a stave fixing the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: Ruler?

parts.note: not a monarch but something or someone that draws lines

explanation.definitionFit: One who rules lines, also a ship or eyeliner pencil; here the line-drawer.

clue.text: Loquacious lecture at teatime perhaps by expedition leader

parts.note: to talk is to lecture
taken as written
four o'clock is a traditional teatime, and four is IV in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the leader of expedition is its first letter

explanation.surface: A chatty speech given at teatime by the head of an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: Teatime in Britain is traditionally around four o'clock, hence IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Given to a lot of chatter; garrulous.

clue.text: Time to retire-eventually

definitions.meaning: the evening, when one goes to bed
ultimately, when all is said and done

explanation.definitionFit: Literally evening, bedtime; idiomatically, ultimately or when everything is considered.
